<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Rohingya conflict]]
**Three [[Tatmadaw|military]] officers are found guilty of atrocities against the [[Rohingya people|Rohingya]] by a [[court-martial]] in [[Myanmar]]. No details were provided on the perpetrators, their crimes, or their sentences. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/myanmar-finds-troops-guilty-rohingya-atrocities-court-martial-200630101738034.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Afghan peace process]]
**[[Taliban]] spokesman Suhail Shaheen says on [[Twitter]] that there was a [[videoconference]] on Monday between [[U.S. Secretary of State]] [[Mike Pompeo]] and Taliban official [[Mullah Baradar]] to discuss the peace process. The group reiterated its commitments to not attack [[United States Armed Forces|American personnel]], to engage in intra-Afghan talks and "not let anyone to use its soil to attack other countries". The meeting was confirmed by the [[U.S. State Department]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-taliban-usa/u-s-taliban-say-afghan-peace-effort-discussed-in-video-talks-idUSKBN24112P?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Mali War]]
**The [[United Nations Security Council]] votes unanimously to extend the mandate of [[United Nations Multidimensional Integrated Stabilization Mission in Mali|MINUSMA]], the [[United Nations peacekeeping]] force in [[Mali]], until June 30, 2021. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-06/30/c_139177413.htm (Xinhuanet)]

;Arts and culture
*[[List of monuments and memorials removed during the George Floyd protests]]
**A vandalized statue of former [[Monarchy of Belgium|King]] [[Leopold II of Belgium]] is removed from public display in the city of [[Ghent]] amid anti-racism protests. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-07-01/belgium-removes-king-leopold-congo-independence-black-lives/12408672 (ABC News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*A large explosion at a medical clinic in [[Tehran]], [[Iran]], kills at least 19 people, mostly women, according to Iranian authorities. A [[gas leak]] is suspected as being the cause. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-53239170 (BBC News)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Georgia (U.S. state)|COVID-19 pandemic in Georgia]]
****[[List of mayors of Savannah, Georgia|Savannah Mayor]] [[Van R. Johnson]] orders residents to wear masks in public as cases surge. [https://thehill.com/homenews/state-watch/505423-georgia-mayor-orders-residents-to-wear-masks-in-public (''The Hill'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Massachusetts]]
****[[Massachusetts]] reports no COVID-19 deaths for the first time in months. [https://www.bostonglobe.com/2020/06/30/nation/mass-reports-zero-new-coronavirus-deaths-first-time-months/ (''Boston Globe'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
***The COVID-19 death toll in [[Mexico]] reaches to 28,000, surpassing [[Spain]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-mexico-tally/mexico-coronavirus-death-toll-hits-28510-exceeding-spain-reuters-tally-idUSKBN24301W (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
***[[Fiji]] [[quarantine]]s 160 [[peacekeeping]] [[Republic of Fiji Military Forces|soldiers]] who returned from the [[Middle East]] on Saturday after the army had expressed concern that some of the troops may have been in contact with infected people. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/420195/fijian-troops-under-strict-covid-19-watch (RNZ)]

;International relations
*[[India–Pakistan relations]]; [[2020 Pakistan Stock Exchange attack]]
**[[Pakistani Prime Minister|Prime Minister]] [[Imran Khan]] says "There is no doubt that [[India]] is behind the attack" on the [[Pakistan Stock Exchange]] yesterday. India rebuffs the accusation and says it had nothing to do with the assault. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-pakistan-attacks/pakistani-pm-says-no-doubt-that-india-was-behind-stock-exchange-attack-idUSKBN2411RB?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Belgium–Democratic Republic of the Congo relations]]
**In a letter to [[President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|President]] [[Felix Tshisekedi]], King [[Philippe of Belgium]] addresses the [[atrocities in the Congo Free State]] under the rule of [[King Leopold II]]: "I would like to express my deepest regrets for the wounds of the past, the pain of today, which is rekindled by the discrimination all too present in our society." [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jun/30/belgian-king-philippe-expresses-profound-regrets-for-brutal-colonial-rule (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Latvia–Russia relations]]
**[[Latvia]] bans seven channels belonging to [[Russian state]]-run news network [[RT (TV network)|RT]], claiming it was trying to present the country as a [[failed state]]. [[Dmitry Kiselyov]], head of the separate Russian state-run news agency [[Rossiya Segodnya]], dismisses the claim and accuses the [[Latvian government]] of [[Anti-Russian sentiment#Latvia|Russophobia]] in its ruling. [https://apnews.com/0c6cf24233c7097d4d7bd89697894a60 (AP News)]

;Law and crime
*[[2017–2018 Iranian protests]]
**A court in [[Iran]] sentences former journalist and activist [[Ruhollah Zam]] to death for fueling anti-[[government of Iran|government]] unrest in late 2017 on [[social media]]. He was convicted of being [[Mofsed-e-filarz|corrupt on Earth]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iran-journalist-verdict/iran-sentences-former-journalist-to-death-for-fuelling-unrest-idUSKBN2411Q8 (Reuters)]
*[[2020 boogaloo killings]] 
**[[Facebook]] bans groups affiliated with the [[boogaloo movement]], which was linked to a pair of attacks in [[California]], US, that left two dead and three injured earlier this month and late last month. [https://nbc25news.com/news/nation-world/facebook-bans-violent-boogaloo-groups-not-the-term-itself (AP via WEYI-TV)]
*Police in [[Vatican City]] raid the department in charge of the maintenance and restoration of [[St. Peter's Basilica]]. The raid came due to suspicion of corruption in the awarding of building [[contract]]s. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/vatican-police-carry-raid-suspected-corruption-200630104123086.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Vietnam]]'s [[civil aviation]] authority grounds all [[Pakistan]]i pilots flying for Vietnamese airlines, as global aviation regulators respond to revelations by Pakistani authorities that more than 250 pilots obtaining licences fraudulently. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/vietnam-suspends-pakistani-pilots-suspect-licences-200630071937493.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Hong Kong national security law|Hong Kong national security law]]
**[[China]] passes the controversial [[2020 Hong Kong national security law|Hong Kong national security law]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/06/29/world/asia/china-hong-kong-security-law-rules.html (''The New York Times'')]
**The political party [[Demosistō]] of social activist [[Joshua Wong]] is disbanded following the passing of the law. Wong urges the international community to keep "speaking up for Hong Kong people". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-hongkong-protests-wong/hong-kong-democracy-activist-group-led-by-joshua-wong-disbands-idUSKBN2410C6?il=0 (Reuters)]
*Demonstrations break out in [[Addis Ababa]], Ethiopia, following the shooting death of protest singer [[Hachalu Hundessa]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-53233531 (BBC News)]
*[[Government of Germany|German]] [[Federal Ministry of Defence (Germany)|Defence Minister]] [[Annegret Kramp-Karrenbauer]] orders the "partial dissolution" of the country's elite ''[[Kommando Spezialkräfte]]'' (KSK) special forces command over its suspected ties to the [[Far-right politics in Germany (1945–present)|far-right]]. The KSK also has a "toxic leadership culture", according to the Defence Minister. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-53237685 (BBC News)]
*[[Mississippi]] governor [[Tate Reeves]] signs a bill into legislation abandoning the [[flag of Mississippi|state's flag]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/national/mississippi-flag-confederacy-removed/2020/06/30/f47df152-baed-11ea-8cf5-9c1b8d7f84c6_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]

;Sports
*[[Reactions to the George Floyd protests]]
**The [[Premier League]] reaffirms its support of the [[Black Lives Matter]] movement, saying it was not political but moral support and that it was "aware of the risk posed by groups that seek to hijack popular causes and campaigns". It comes after one group, UKBLM, received widespread criticism for calling for the dismantling of [[capitalism]], and tweeted "Free [[Palestinian territories|Palestine]]". [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-england-politics/premier-league-says-support-for-black-lives-matter-not-political-idUKKBN241262 (Reuters)]
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]]
**[[Minor League Baseball]] cancels its 2020 season due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/06/30/us/minor-league-baseball-spt-trnd/index.html (CNN)]
